_readme: Door metadata for the portal (assets/codex.js). Keys are matched case-insensitively against the door index built from LEX + the glossary. Fields: world = visual family (mind|wire|silicon|shield|craft|world), art = images/ path shown in the room, why = one line on why the operator should care, kin = neighboring doors to walk to. Every field is optional; the door works without this file. The caretaker never touches it — edit by hand.

token.why: Every bill, speed and memory limit you will ever hit is counted in these.

context window.why: When it fills, the model genuinely forgets — every long chat you have ever had degraded because of this.

quantization.why: The one trick that puts a real model on your Pi instead of in someone else's datacenter.

agent.why: The shift of the decade: software that acts is a different animal from software that answers.

mcp.why: The socket your future tools will plug into — and a new supply chain to audit.

rag.why: The difference between a model that guesses about your documents and one that cites them.

lora.why: Fine-tuning for the price of a takeaway — your voice, your formats, on an open model.

prompt injection.why: The attack class that makes an over-powered agent dangerous to its own owner.

egress.why: The single highest-leverage control you can put around an agent — watch what leaves, not what arrives.

embedding.why: How meaning becomes geometry — the trick underneath every 'search by meaning' feature you use.

vector store.why: Your Pi can hold hundreds of thousands of memories and answer 'what is near this?' in milliseconds.

inference.why: This is the electricity bill of AI — training happens once, inference happens every single time.

hallucination.why: Confidence tells you nothing about truth — design around it or be burned by it.

transformer.why: One architecture ate the whole field — everything above this layer runs on it.

container.why: The reason 'works on my machine' stopped being an excuse — and the standard box agents get run in.

ssh.why: The key to your node from anywhere on earth — and the first door attackers rattle.

dns.why: The quietest place to catch a compromised machine talking to its master.

tls.why: Free, automatic, and the reason your traffic is not a postcard — know why the padlock holds.

zero trust.why: The end of 'inside the building means trusted' — every request proves itself, every time.

mfa.why: The strong version — a passkey — makes a perfect fake login page worthless.

ransomware.why: The only reliable answer is a backup that was tested before you needed it.

cve.why: Patch by what is actually being exploited, not by the scariest score.

supply chain attack.why: You audit your own code; who audits the two hundred packages it pulls in?

phishing.why: Still the front door of almost every breach — now written fluently by machines.

systemd.why: The difference between a script you baby-sit and a service that survives a power cut.

cron.why: This very page rebuilds itself on five numbers and a schedule — that is cron.

acid.why: The promise that a power cut mid-save does not corrupt everything you own.

index.why: The difference between a query in milliseconds and a query in minutes is usually one of these.

idempotent.why: Networks lie and everything retries — anything not idempotent eventually double-charges someone.

observability.why: An unmetered agent is an unbounded invoice — instrument cost before anything else.

eval.why: The only way to change a prompt without arguing from vibes.

post-quantum.why: Secrets recorded today can be unlocked by a machine that does not exist yet — the migration already started.

edge.why: Instant everywhere, but tiny and forgetful — know which of your jobs fit inside it.

webhook.why: The doorbell pattern — and the whole argument for keeping one machine always awake.

git.why: Perfect memory for a project — committed is saved, pushed is safe.

api.why: The front counter every service offers machines — and where your keys must never leak.

kernel.why: Everything your machine does passes through this one gatekeeper.

nat.why: The accidental firewall your home lives behind — and why overlays beat opening ports.

reverse proxy.why: One hardened front door instead of a dozen open windows.

sbom.why: When the midnight advisory lands, this is the difference between 'we are fine' and a week of panic.

gdpr.why: Personal data belongs to the person — your agents need to log what left the building, and why.

ai act.why: Sorted by harm, not cleverness — know which tier your use case lands in before you ship it.

ollama.why: One command and the model is yours — no account, no meter, no data leaving the house.

test-time compute.why: The industry's current bet: thinking longer beats building bigger.

hbm.why: The real bottleneck of the AI age is not compute — it is feeding the chip.

euv.why: One company, one machine, every advanced chip on earth — the chokepoint everything else orbits.

diffusion.why: Every generated image you have ever seen is noise, removed carefully.

orchestration.why: Management, applied to software that thinks — and the reason deterministic scripts still run the show.

arm.why: The architecture in your phone, your Pi, and increasingly the datacenter — efficiency won.

branch.why: Several drafts of the truth, alive at once, without fear.

commit.why: A numbered snapshot you can return to forever — the unit of never losing work again.

continual learning.why: The unsolved problem: models that learn after training without forgetting what they knew.

ci/cd.why: Machines checking your work on every push — this page deploys itself the same way.

env var.why: Where secrets live so they never end up in the repo.

event-driven.why: Nothing polls, everything reacts — cheaper, faster, and how the caretaker hears about the world.

export controls.why: Geopolitics conducted in nanometres — who may buy which chip shapes the whole field.

gpu.why: Thousands of slow workers beat four fast ones at exactly the maths AI is made of.

llm.why: A machine that plays one game — guess the next word-piece — well enough to look like thought.

open-weights.why: The dials are public — run it, tune it, own it; the frontier stays rented.

pr.why: The unit of review — where changes get argued about before they become the truth.

proxy.why: A stand-in on the wire — for privacy, for filtering, or for pretending to be somewhere else.

push.why: Committed is saved on your machine; pushed is safe on someone else's.

rebase.why: Rewriting history so it reads as if you were never confused — with new serial numbers to prove it.

residential ip.why: Traffic that looks like a house, not a datacenter — the cat-and-mouse currency of scraping.

shadow ai.why: The AI your organisation does not know it is using — the compliance gap walking in through the side door.

bearer token.why: Whoever holds it, is you. Treat every one like a signed blank cheque.

edge function.why: Code in two hundred cities with a ten-second attention span — brilliant for some jobs, fatal for others.

egress allowlist.why: A short list of doors an agent may knock on — everything else becomes a logged, blocked attempt.

fingerprint.why: You are recognisable without cookies — your browser's quirks are the cookie.

fuzzing.why: Throw a million malformed inputs at it before an attacker throws the one that matters.

hmac.why: How a webhook proves it really came from the service and not from anyone with your URL.

idor.why: Change the number in the URL, see someone else's data — the oldest boring catastrophe on the web.

ja3/ja4.why: Your TLS handshake is a signature — servers know what is calling before a single header arrives.

model collapse.why: Models trained on model output forget the tails — the ouroboros problem of a synthetic web.

sandbox.why: Let the untrusted thing run — inside walls you chose, with nothing valuable in reach.

serverless.why: No machine to patch at 2am — and a cold start tax every time nobody was asking.

service worker.why: The page's agent in the browser — offline, caching, and push, all live here.

signature.why: Maths that proves who wrote it and that nobody changed it since.

vector database.why: Millions of meaning-points, queried by nearness, in milliseconds — memory for machines.

c2pa.why: Provenance stapled to pixels — the counterweight to a world where any image can be conjured.

cgnat.why: Thousands of homes behind one address — the reason your server cannot be reached, and the overlay is the answer.

cia triad.why: Every security decision you will ever make trades these three against each other.

context engineering.why: The craft that replaced prompt magic: curating what the model sees, not begging it nicely.

cowos.why: The packaging step nobody had heard of that gates the world's accelerator supply.

dcb0129.why: The clinical-safety standard that decides whether your NHS-adjacent software is allowed to exist.

dpia.why: The risk assessment you do before the processing, not after the complaint.

epss.why: The probability a flaw is exploited in the wild — patch by this, not by drama.

kev.why: Not 'could be exploited' — is being exploited, right now. The list you patch first.

latency.why: The tax distance charges every request — the reason regions exist and edges multiplied.

least privilege.why: Give everything the minimum it needs — so a compromise stays a incident, not a catastrophe.

migration.why: Schema changes as versioned, reversible steps — the difference between evolution and surgery on a live patient.

owasp top 10.why: The ten ways web apps actually get owned — read it once and stop making the classic mistakes.

passkey.why: A secret your device only ever reveals to the real website — phishing dies by construction.

port.why: Doors in the address — every open one is a promise something is listening.

schema.why: The agreed shape of the data — and with structured output, the leash that keeps a model's answer parseable.

sqlite.why: A whole database in one file, no server — right answer for almost everything on a node.

structured output.why: Force the answer into a schema and the model becomes a component instead of a conversation.

tcp.why: The handshake, the ordering, the retries — the politeness protocol everything reliable rides on.

threat model.why: Who would attack you, how, and for what — decide this before buying any defence.

udp.why: No handshake, no promises, no waiting — why your video call survives and your download would not.

vla.why: Vision-language-action: the models that stopped describing the world and started moving in it.

wireguard.why: A private wire between your machines across any network — the modern answer to 'how do I reach home?'

world model.why: The bet that prediction of the world, not of text, is the road to the next leap.

accessibility.why: Built right, the page works for everyone — and the same structure is what agents read too.

base rate.why: The reason a 99% accurate alarm is mostly false alarms — the trap under every metric.

cascade.why: Small failure, systemwide consequence — the shape of most famous outages, and of agent error compounding.

egress fee.why: Data checks in free and pays to leave — the quiet lock-in of every cloud bill.

flaky test.why: A test you cannot trust is worse than no test — it teaches you to ignore red.

iam.why: Who may do what — the cloud's entire security model, and where most cloud breaches actually start.

iaas/paas/saas.why: Bare machine, platform, or product — what you rent decides what you patch.

precision.why: Of everything you flagged, how much was real — the other half of every detector's story.

recall.why: Of everything real, how much you caught — tune it against precision, never alone.

reflow.why: The page shoving itself around as things load — measured, penalised, and entirely preventable.

region.why: Where your data physically sleeps — a latency choice, a legal choice, and a bill choice at once.

semantic html.why: Tags that say what things are — screen readers, search engines and agents all read the same skeleton.

shared responsibility.why: The cloud secures the building; what you do in your room is yours — most breaches live in that gap.

static typing.why: Whole categories of bug caught before the program ever runs — armour you write once.

training.why: School, apprenticeship, manners — the three-stage forge every model you meet was hammered in.

firewall.why: The bouncer at both doors — and the egress half is the one most people forget to staff.

backup.why: Three copies, two media, one off-site — and none of it counts until a restore has been rehearsed.

cpu.why: Four brilliant workers — unbeatable at winding roads, outnumbered on the flat.

ram.why: The desk everything must fit on — the ceiling for every model your node can hold.

packet.why: Everything you send is diced into these — reassembled, retried, and routed without ceremony.

tool.why: The hinge of the agentic era — the moment a model stops describing and starts doing.
